library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kitabi_2018_efavirenz"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kitabi_2018_efavirenz"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-018-34674-3> (open access; the
  Supplementary Information holds the NONMEM control stream of the final model)

# Population

Kitabi 2018 enrolled 56 treatment-naive Tanzanian adults with HIV and CD4
counts below 200 cells/uL at Muhimbili National Hospital, Dar es Salaam. Arm 1
(n = 20, HIV only) started efavirenz 600 mg once daily with lamivudine and
zidovudine, stavudine or tenofovir, and gave an intensive steady-state profile
at week 16. Arm 2 (n = 36, HIV with tuberculosis) started rifampicin,
isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol and added the same antiretroviral
regimen 4 weeks later; it gave intensive profiles at week 20 of anti-TB therapy
(about 16 weeks of efavirenz) and again at week 32, 8 weeks after anti-TB
therapy ended. Samples were drawn at about 0, 1, 3, 6, 12, 16 and 24 h after an
evening dose; all 556 concentrations were above the 10 ng/mL limit of
quantification. Median (IQR) age was 42 (36-50) years and weight 48 (43-60) kg.
Arm 1 was 75% female with mean weight 45.5 kg; arm 2 was 36% female with mean
weight 55.1 kg (Table 1). CYP2B6 c.516G>T (\*6) genotype was available for 37
subjects: \*1/\*1 18, \*1/\*6 13, \*6/\*6 6 (Table 1).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Kitabi_2018_efavirenz")()$population`.

# Source trace

| `lvc` (V/F, 70 kg) | log(209) L | Table 2 'V'; stream THETA(2) |
| `lka` | log(0.344) 1/h | Table 2 'KA'; stream THETA(3) |
| `lq` (Q/F, 70 kg) | log(59.2) L/h | Table 2 'Q'; stream THETA(4) |
| `lvp` (VP/F, 70 kg) | log(912) L | Table 2 'VP'; stream THETA(5) |
| `e_wt_cl_q` | 0.75 (fixed) | Methods; stream LTVCL and MU_4 |
| `e_wt_vc_vp` | 1 (fixed) | stream LTVV and MU_5 |

| `e_tb_cyp2b6_6wt_cl` | 0.915 | Table 2 'theta211'; stream THETA(10) |
| `e_tb_cyp2b6_6het_cl` | 0.852 | Table 2 'theta212'; stream THETA(11) |
| `e_tb_cyp2b6_6hom_cl` | 1.02 | Table 2 'theta213'; stream THETA(12) |
| `e_occ2_cyp2b6_6wt_cl` | 1.19 | Table 2 'phi221'; stream THETA(13) |

# Typical-value clearance check

Equation (3) makes CL/F a product of genotype, arm and occasion fractions. The
table below recomputes the typical CL/F of a 70 kg woman in every stratum from
the packaged model and compares it to the product of the Table 2 estimates.
Both sides use the same parameters, so the agreement must be exact.

```{r typical-cl}
mod <- readModelDb("Kitabi_2018_efavirenz")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

strata <- tibble::tribble(
  ~stratum,              ~TB_POS, ~OCC,
  "Arm 1 EFV (WK16)",    0,       1,
  "Arm 2 RIF/EFV (WK20)", 1,      1,
  "Arm 2 EFV (WK32)",    1,       2
) |>
  tidyr::crossing(SNP_CYP2B6_RS3745274_T_COUNT = 0:2)

ev_typ <- strata |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number(), time = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central",
                WT = 70, SEXF = 1)

typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_typ,
                       keep = c("stratum", "SNP_CYP2B6_RS3745274_T_COUNT")) |>
  as.data.frame()

expected <- strata |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    geno = c(1, 0.618, 0.311)[SNP_CYP2B6_RS3745274_T_COUNT + 1],
    arm = ifelse(TB_POS == 1, c(0.915, 0.852, 1.02)[SNP_CYP2B6_RS3745274_T_COUNT + 1], 1),
    occ = ifelse(TB_POS == 1 & OCC == 2, c(1.19, 1.19, 1.05)[SNP_CYP2B6_RS3745274_T_COUNT + 1], 1),
    cl_expected = 23.4 * geno * arm * occ
  )

cl_tab <- typ |>
  dplyr::select(stratum, SNP_CYP2B6_RS3745274_T_COUNT, cl) |>
  dplyr::left_join(expected, by = c("stratum", "SNP_CYP2B6_RS3745274_T_COUNT")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(genotype = c("*1/*1", "*1/*6", "*6/*6")[SNP_CYP2B6_RS3745274_T_COUNT + 1])

stopifnot(all(abs(cl_tab$cl / cl_tab$cl_expected - 1) < 1e-8))

cl_tab |>
  dplyr::select(stratum, genotype, cl, cl_expected) |>
  dplyr::mutate(genotype = gsub("*", "\\*", genotype, fixed = TRUE)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Stratum" = stratum, "CYP2B6 genotype" = genotype,
    "Model CL/F (L/h)" = cl, "Table 2 product (L/h)" = cl_expected
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical CL/F for a 70 kg woman.")
```

The derived percentages match the Results: CL/F is 38% (1 - 0.618) and 69%
(1 - 0.311) lower for CYP2B6\*1/\*6 and \*6/\*6 than for \*1/\*1 in arm 1; during
anti-TB co-treatment the \*1/\*6 stratum is 15% lower than in arm 1
(0.852), and after co-treatment the \*1/\*1 stratum is 19% higher than during it
(1.19).

# Virtual cohort

Each arm gets 200 virtual subjects. Weight is drawn from a normal distribution
with the arm's Table 1 mean and SD, redrawing values outside 30-100 kg; sex
follows the arm's Table 1 split. Genotype frequencies combine the observed
genotypes of Table 1 with the subjects the mixture model assigned (Results:
2 arm-1 and 13 arm-2 subjects with missing genotype to \*1/\*1, and 2 in each
arm to \*6/\*6), giving \*1/\*1 : \*1/\*6 : \*6/\*6 = 9 : 7 : 4 in arm 1 and
24 : 6 : 6 in arm 2. Arm-2 subjects are simulated on both occasions with the
same between-subject etas and independent between-occasion etas.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2018)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2018)

draw_wt <- function(n, mean, sd) {
  wt <- rnorm(n, mean, sd)
  bad <- wt < 30 | wt > 100
  while (any(bad)) {
    wt[bad] <- rnorm(sum(bad), mean, sd)
    bad <- wt < 30 | wt > 100
  }
  wt
}

n_arm <- 200
obs_times <- seq(0, 24, by = 0.5)

make_subjects <- function(n, tb_pos, wt_mean, wt_sd, p_female, p_geno, id_offset) {
  tibble::tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    TB_POS = tb_pos,
    WT = draw_wt(n, wt_mean, wt_sd),
    SEXF = rbinom(n, 1, p_female),
    SNP_CYP2B6_RS3745274_T_COUNT = sample(0:2, n, replace = TRUE, prob = p_geno)
  )
}

# One steady-state dosing occasion starting at `t0`.
make_occasion <- function(subj, occ, t0, label) {
  dose <- subj |>
    dplyr::mutate(time = t0, evid = 1, amt = 600, ii = 24, ss = 1, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(tad = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(time = t0 + tad, evid = 0, amt = 0, ii = 0, ss = 0, cmt = "central") |>
    dplyr::select(-tad)
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(OCC = occ, treatment = label, t0 = t0)
}

arm1 <- make_subjects(n_arm, 0, 45.50, 13.15, 15 / 20, c(9, 7, 4) / 20, 0L)
arm2 <- make_subjects(n_arm, 1, 55.14, 13.45, 13 / 36, c(24, 6, 6) / 36, n_arm)

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_occasion(arm1, 1, 0, "Arm 1 EFV (WK16)"),
  make_occasion(arm2, 1, 0, "Arm 2 RIF/EFV (WK20)"),
  make_occasion(arm2, 2, 1000, "Arm 2 EFV (WK32)")
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, events = events,
  keep = c("treatment", "t0", "SNP_CYP2B6_RS3745274_T_COUNT")
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    tad = time - t0,
    genotype = factor(c("CYP2B6*1/*1", "CYP2B6*1/*6", "CYP2B6*6/*6")[SNP_CYP2B6_RS3745274_T_COUNT + 1]),
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c("Arm 1 EFV (WK16)", "Arm 2 RIF/EFV (WK20)", "Arm 2 EFV (WK32)"))
  )
```

# Replicate published figures

```{r figure-3, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Efavirenz concentration (ug/mL)",
       title = "Steady-state profiles, 5th-50th-95th percentiles",
       caption = "Replicates the layout of Figure 3 of Kitabi 2018.")
```

```{r figure-1, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
fig1 <- sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, genotype, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q25 = quantile(Cc, 0.25), Q50 = median(Cc), Q75 = quantile(Cc, 0.75),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(fig1, aes(tad, Q50, colour = genotype, fill = genotype)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q25, ymax = Q75), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Efavirenz concentration (ug/mL)",
       colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "Median and interquartile range by CYP2B6*6 genotype",
       caption = "Compare with the observed medians of Figure 1 of Kitabi 2018.")
```

Figure 1 of the paper shows observed 24 h concentrations near 0.7-1 ug/mL in
CYP2B6\*1/\*1 subjects and near 4-5 ug/mL in \*6/\*6 subjects, with \*1/\*6 in
between, and the three panels look alike. The simulated medians reproduce that
ordering and magnitude. The check below uses wide bands that a mis-transcribed
clearance or a unit error (both of which move the trough several-fold) would
leave, and that sampling variation in a 200-subject cohort will not.

```{r figure-1-check}
trough <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(tad == 24) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, genotype) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median_trough = median(Cc), n = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop")

trough |>
  dplyr::mutate(genotype = gsub("*", "\\*", as.character(genotype), fixed = TRUE)) |>
  dplyr::rename("Stratum" = treatment, "Genotype" = genotype,
                "Median 24 h concentration (ug/mL)" = median_trough, "N" = n) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2,
             caption = "Simulated median 24 h concentration (ug/mL).")

wt_trough <- trough$median_trough[trough$genotype == "CYP2B6*1/*1"]
hom_trough <- trough$median_trough[trough$genotype == "CYP2B6*6/*6"]
stopifnot(
  all(wt_trough > 0.4 & wt_trough < 2),
  all(hom_trough > 2 & hom_trough < 9)
)
```

# PKNCA validation

At steady state the AUC over one 24 h dosing interval equals Dose / (CL/F) for
each subject. PKNCA computes AUC0-24 from the simulated profile; the ratio to
600 / CL/F tests the dosing, the steady-state solve and the units together. The
only difference between the two sides is trapezoidal error on the 0.5 h grid.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(subj = paste(id, treatment)) |>
  dplyr::select(subj, id, treatment, genotype, tad, Cc)

dose_df <- sim_nca |>
  dplyr::distinct(subj, id, treatment, genotype) |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = 0, amt = 600)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ tad | treatment + genotype + subj)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ tad | treatment + genotype + subj)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, genotype, subj, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

cl_subj <- sim |>
  dplyr::mutate(subj = paste(id, treatment)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(subj) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cl = dplyr::first(cl), .groups = "drop")

chk <- nca_wide |>
  dplyr::left_join(cl_subj, by = "subj") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auclast / (600 / cl) - 1))

stopifnot(
  abs(median(chk$pct_diff)) < 2,
  quantile(abs(chk$pct_diff), 0.9) < 5
)

chk |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, genotype) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cmax = median(cmax), tmax = median(tmax), cmin = median(cmin),
    auclast = median(auclast), cl = median(cl), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(genotype = gsub("*", "\\*", as.character(genotype), fixed = TRUE)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Stratum" = treatment, "Genotype" = genotype,
    "Cmax (ug/mL)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax, "Cmin (ug/mL)" = cmin,
    "AUC0-24 (ug*h/mL)" = auclast, "CL/F (L/h)" = cl
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Median simulated steady-state NCA by stratum.")
```

The paper reports no NCA table, so there is no published Cmax or AUC to set
beside these values.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Final estimates.** Table 2 is used for every value. The supplement control
  stream's `$THETA` and `$OMEGA` initial values equal the Table 2 estimates to
  rounding (for example CL 23.3545 vs 23.4, V 208.817 vs 209), so the two
  sources agree. The Results paragraph and abstract quote different values
  (CL/F 23.6 L/h, KA 0.37 1/h, V/F 314 L, Q/F 68 and VP/F 947 L) that match
  neither Table 2 nor the final run in Supplementary Table S1; Table 2 is
  used.
- **CL/F-V/F covariance.** Table 2 prints only the variances. The control
  stream estimates them as `$OMEGA BLOCK(2)` with covariance 0.300906
  (correlation about 0.98); that covariance is used with the Table 2
  variances.
- **VP/F variability** was fixed to 0 in the final model and is omitted.
- **Between-occasion variability** applies only to the HIV/TB arm (control
  stream `BOVCL = 1` unless GROUP is 21 or 22), with one eta per occasion
  sharing the Table 2 variance 0.0934925 (the stream's value is 0.093522).
- **Additive residual error unit.** Table 2 labels 'ADD' in ug/L, but the
  concentrations are in ug/mL (Figure 1 axis; the model scales the central
  amount in mg by V/F in L), so `addSd` is 0.0873 mg/L.
- **Table 2 row labels.** The rows for theta213 and phi223 both say
  'CYP2B6\*1/\*6'; equation (3) and the control stream (THETA(12) and THETA(15)
  are the 'CP2B3' terms) make them the \*6/\*6 fractions.
- **Results text vs Table 2.** The Results say CL/F in \*1/\*1 subjects was 10%
  lower during co-treatment than in arm 1 (Table 2: 0.915, 8.5% lower) and
  that CL/F rose 5% after co-treatment in \*1/\*6 subjects (Table 2 and the
  stream: 1.19 for \*1/\*6 and 1.05 for \*6/\*6). The model follows Table 2 and
  the stream. The Results also attribute both mixture proportions (78% and
  22%) to \*1/\*1; the second is \*6/\*6 (stream: P(1) = 0.784, P(2) fixed to 0,
  P(3) = 1 - P(1)).
- **Missing-genotype mixture.** The authors imputed missing CYP2B6\*6
  genotypes with a NONMEM `$MIX` model. The packaged model takes genotype as a
  covariate; the mixture probabilities are recorded in the covariate's notes
  for users who need to impute.
- **Arm and occasion covariates.** The arm indicator A2 is carried as `TB_POS`
  (HIV/TB patients) and occasion 2 as `OCC = 2`. The arm-2 fractions combine
  TB disease and the rifampicin/isoniazid co-medication, which this design
  cannot separate.
- **Virtual cohort.** Weights are drawn from normal distributions with the
  Table 1 arm means and SDs, limited to 30-100 kg by redrawing. Genotype
  frequencies use the observed genotypes plus the mixture-model assignments
  reported in the Results. Each arm-2 subject is simulated on both occasions.
- No erratum or correction for this article was found on Europe PMC
  (checked 2026-11-25).
